name: s2-shape
shape: static site in a subfolder behind Caddy with browser timers, a build script writing html, a tools script writing json, Firebase Functions 2nd gen, an iOS app

platform.name: Unknown
platform.why: the site's host is configured outside the repository (no railway.json, render.yaml, fly.toml or vercel.json); the agent finds it with the host's CLI

processes.note: Caddy (website/Caddyfile) serves website/dist, which website/build.py writes in the image's build stage; listens on $PORT

stays.note: signup (onRequest) and dailyCount (onSchedule) from firebase-functions/v2, deployed by firebase.json; they already run on Cloud Run functions and Cloud Scheduler

data.note: the functions write signups and stats with firebase-admin; already on Google

notBreaks.why: browser code: a carousel's setInterval in a file Caddy serves as a static asset
static site generator: writes html into dist/ while the image is built
a local tool that rebuilds the catalog the iOS app ships with
onSchedule is Cloud Scheduler calling a function, not a timer inside a process
iOS app source: a Timer on the phone
iOS app source: writes to the phone's documents folder

notes: Reproduces the shape of a real session (SPEC F7, S2) without its content: every name and line here is made up. A correct audit finds one web process (the static site), two functions that stay, no breaks, names website/start/, website/build.py, tools/ and ios/ as not on the server, and asks for the platform. The site's form posts to the signup function, so the site and the functions are two parts of one product.
